'''Nandini Kannan''' is the Executive Director at the [[United States-India Science & Technology Endowment Fund|Indo-U.S. Science and Technology Forum (IUSSTF)]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=IUSSTF - Indo-U.S. Science and Technology Forum|url=https://www.iusstf.org/|access-date=2021-04-25|website=IUSSTF.Org|language=en}}</ref> and also Dean of Academics & Director of Data Science Institute at Plaksha University.

==Education and career==

Kannan received her PhD in Statistics from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1992. Her dissertation, Estimation of Direction of Arrival in Signal Processing Models, was supervised by [[C. R. Rao]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=49071}}</ref>

Kannan spent over 20 years in academia, first as a faculty member and then as Chair, Department of Management Science and Statistics at the [[University of Texas at San Antonio|University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA)]]. During her time at UTSA, she helped to develop new undergraduate and graduate programs and led a university-wide initiative on [[quantitative literacy]]. Since 2014, Kannan has served as a Program Director at the [[National Science Foundation|US National Science Foundation (NSF)]] where her responsibilities included core disciplinary research, mathematical sciences research institutes, and workforce development programs in the Division of Mathematical Sciences as well as a number of cross-directorate and cross-agency activities.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nandini Kannan {{!}} NSF - National Science Foundation|url=https://www.nsf.gov/staff/staff_bio.jsp?lan=nakannan&org=NSF|access-date=2021-04-25|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref> She has served as a co-chair for several [[Data science|Data Science]] related activities in support of Harnessing the Data Revolution, one of NSF’s 10 Big Ideas. She helped to create new programs to support data science foundations as well as data-intensive research in different science and engineering domains. Kannan also helped to create partnerships with the [[National Institutes of Health|National Institutes of Health (NIH)]] to support collaborative efforts in biomedical data science. She serves on the board of trustees of the International Indian Statistical Association (IISA) and is a former President of IISA.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Nandini Kannan|url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2021/03/01/nandini-kannan/|access-date=2021-04-25|website=magazine.amstat.org}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

Kannan was awarded the [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS Fellows Award]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=2019 AAAS Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/AWM-News-NovDec-2020-PRINT.pdf|journal=Association for Women in Mathematics Newsletter|volume=50|pages=19}}</ref>
